Name:  
Xaver Aisenpreis

I don't think that his life is completely controlled by fate and fortune. I would say his life is pre-scripted but not in detail. Arthur is in the wheel of fortune like any other person on earth. For example, he starts as somebody unknown to the public. Later, the wheel rotates, and he becomes the king. Later, many knights fight him and he struggles, but in the end he gets the Grail with his friend and wins. This shows that his fortune changes every time.

Fate is what happens in your life that you can't change it. His fights, for example, were a fixed part of the plan of God. He can't control fate, but he can control his actions. He chooses to be brave, fair, and kind. Arthur's power is not just his sword or army, but his goodness. The story shows that a good king like him stays strong and fair when fortune turns. And fate tests people, but wisdom and virtue decides who they really are.

That's why I don't think that Arthur is controlled by fortune or fate. Fate and fortune happens, but he controls how it affects him by his actions.

Name: Synthia Salazar  

In the story, Fate was explained as an eternal and temporal unfolding sequence of events, the chain that governs the physical world and human affairs as they play out over time. I think it is the servant for the gods.  

Fortune is the unpredictable aspect of fate as a "plan" to happen. Fortune is the ups and downs of life, things like power, fame, and health are things that can come and go unerringly. The story described fortune using the metaphor of the "Wheel of Fortune." When you look at the meaning of "The Wheel of Fortune," everything on that wheel is not permanent; you get to the top, but it is just temporary.  

Following this, I think that Arthur is controlled by fate and fortune. I think this because he had many experiences following his fate to becoming king. When Arthur was born, he was already fated to be king because of his father, and everything led to him finding his fate. I think that finding Arthur was part of his fate.  

When Arthur was born and given to Ector, Arthur didn't know he was the king; he was raised as a commoner. He only knew because he could pull the sword. I think this was the turning point of his life because this showed how he was superior over everyone else. Overall, there were many things that led to Arthur being king just by him being born, and it was unexpected, so this is fate and fortune. Unexpected power was his destiny.

### The Legend of King Arthur: Fate and Fortune

**By Mason Fisher**

In the legend of King Arthur, both fate and fortune play key roles in his rise to power. My story begins with King Uther, Arthur's father, who sought the sword in the stone after his death. Uther's fate was controlled by fortune, and with his blessing as king, he was buried in the church where people from all over would come to see it.

Arthur's first try at lifting the sword was easy. He pulled it out effortlessly from the crowded yard, and that was pure fate. He became the rightful king. Next is Arthur's other trials, full of doubts and battles against him. Fortune turned against him at times, with everyone questioning his kingship and sages always doubting. Soon there was a fortunate turn when he received Excalibur, which scared his enemies.

It was Arthur's fate to be a great king and defeat others in battle through strength, one wise decision, and wits.

Applying the Concepts of Fate and Fortune

I believe that Arthur is influenced by both fortune and fate. In his early and controlled life, he had fortune in order to pick up his sword in the first place. But in the end, fate chose what happened. First off, it was to win the battle. Fate gave Arthur many signs. Uther, through providence, chooses what happens for the big plan. Uther sent him away and then died, basically giving Arthur the king position with the help of fate. His father, a faithful man—Uther—held the king position. After Arthur was king after pulling the sword out of the stone, I think that was fortune.

Arthur was born at the bottom of the wheel of fortune. But by the wheel of fortune, Uther was at the top. Gaining that availability, I think Uther was on the wheel of fortune when the time he died. He and Arthur rose to the power, but not set back in, and caused right back on because he won the battle and had the top. Soon after hitting the top, fate chose the battle, and God decided his fate and decided to put him back on the wheel of fortune with kid Borre.

Name:  
Deegen  

In my opinion, Arthur's life was controlled by fate and not fortune. His life was lived through an undeniable chain of events, pointing toward fate. In order to live a life of fortune, you must experience the highs and lows on a never-ending cycle. But this concept was never really applied in Arthur's life, and I intend to explain why.  

One could argue that after Arthur is born, he wasn't even poor. He was living in a household with a decent knight, but with ignoble qualities. So if one wanted to prove he lived a life of fortune, this would have to be the lowest point in his life. But on the wheel, I would place it in the middle, not at the lowest. After boyhood, he inherits the king's throne, where he would stay throughout the end of our reading. This would be the very top of the wheel, but really it stops there. His life rose from the middle to the top, and it never changed from that point on. To truly experience fortune, you must go through the highs and lows frequently, and he didn't. Instead, his life was lived through a series of events ordained by a higher power. This explains why his life was lived through fate, and not fortune.  

In conclusion, many examples and evidence have been provided as to why Arthur's life was lived through fate, not fortune. Fortune requires a never-ending change from high points to low points. And fate is just what is set to happen in your life. Overall, this concludes why Arthur's life was controlled by fate.
